title: Nocturnal Animals
keyIdea: Nocturnal animals are active at night and usually asleep in the day. Many have big eyes, big ears or sensitive whiskers to find food in the dark. Owls, bats and hedgehogs are nocturnal; not every animal sleeps when the sun goes down.
familyTip: After dark, listen for an owl or spot a moth by a porch light. Ask: 'Is this animal awake at night? What might help it in the dark?' Compare with a robin you see in the morning.

visual.caption: Nocturnal idea or not? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: owl hunts when it is dark
robin sings in bright morning sun
bat uses hearing in the dark

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort night animals, define nocturnal, match dark-time adaptations, catch the all-sleep myth, name three, then challenge.

kid: Nocturnal means awake and busy at night.
Owls, bats and hedgehogs often move when we sleep.
Big eyes, big ears or whiskers help them find food in the dark.
Not every animal sleeps at night — that idea is a myth.
adult: KS1 science: nocturnal means active at night. Day animals are awake in the day. Words: nocturnal, night, day, owl, bat, hedgehog, eyes, ears, whiskers.
Common mistakes: thinking every animal sleeps at night; calling a robin nocturnal; saying bright feathers help at night.
In the lab your child sorts owl and bat from robin and butterfly, picks the meaning, matches eyes ears whiskers, rejects the sleep myth, names three night animals, then tries challenge traps.
